bib.title: Test-Time Training with Self-Supervision for Generalization under Distribution Shifts

question: Can a model improve under distribution shift by updating its parameters on each unlabeled test sample through a self-supervised auxiliary task before predicting?
hypothesis: Test-time updates on a self-supervised task help the main task when the gradients of the two losses are positively correlated.
contributions: Test-Time Training: turn a single unlabeled test sample into a self-supervised learning problem and update parameters before predicting, with an online variant that keeps state
Improvements on CIFAR-10-C, ImageNet-C, VID-Robust and CIFAR-10.1 without hurting the original distribution
Theory for convex models: positive gradient correlation between main and auxiliary losses guarantees improvement (Theorem 1), supported empirically (Fig 4)

method.summary: A Y-shaped ResNet (shared feature extractor, main branch, rotation-prediction branch) is trained jointly on classification and 4-way rotation prediction. At test time the shared layers are fine-tuned by SGD on the rotation loss of the single test image (augmented copies), then the image is classified; the online variant carries parameters across the test stream.

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.preprocessing: random crop and random horizontal flip

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.size: 1.2M train; 50K validation images used as test

datasets.name: CIFAR-10-C / ImageNet-C
datasets.size: 15 corruption types x 5 severity levels, copies of the test sets
datasets.split: train on original training set only

datasets.name: VID-Robust
datasets.size: 1109 sets of video frames in 30 classes; results on anchor frames
datasets.split: ImageNet model, max-conversion of 1000 to 30 classes; 7 CIFAR-overlap classes rescaled to CIFAR size for the CIFAR model

models.name: ResNet-26 (CIFAR-10)
models.architecture: ResNet with Group Normalization, Y-structure; three groups, shared extractor split at end of second group; self-supervised branch same architecture as main branch except output dim

models.name: ResNet-18 (ImageNet)
models.architecture: ResNet with Group Normalization; four groups, split at end of third group

training.objective: Joint: mean of l_m(x,y;theta_m,theta_e) + l_s(x;theta_s,theta_e), cross-entropy main task plus 4-way rotation (0, 90, 180, 270 degrees) prediction, losses summed with equal weight
training.optimizer: SGD, 'standard hyper-parameters as (Huang et al., 2016; He et al., 2016a)' (values not given)
training.regularisation: Group Normalization instead of Batch Normalization
training.seeds: 'multiple independent trials' for the 0.2% original-set gain; number not stated

other.note: joint-training hyperparameters deferred to cited works; only the last-epoch lr (0.001) is stated

inference.samples: Standard TTT: 10 gradient steps per test image, parameters reset after each prediction. TTT-Online: 1 step per new image, parameters carried over; accuracy averaged over whole shuffled test set.

parameters.test_time_optimizer: SGD, lr 0.001 (last-epoch training lr), weight decay 0, momentum 0
parameters.batch_for_update: batch of augmented copies of the single test image (random crop + horizontal flip); batch size not stated
parameters.appendix_variant: 1 iteration with lr 0.01 gave results 'almost as good' (preliminary)
parameters.cost: 2 x batch size x number of iterations slower than a single forward pass

metrics.name: test error
metrics.definition: classification error on the shifted test set

baselines: Object recognition task only (plain ResNet, GN)
Joint training (Hendrycks et al. 2019a), model fixed at test time
UDA-SS (Sun et al. 2019), treated as an oracle with access to the full unlabeled test set
Adversarial Logit Pairing (Kannan et al. 2018), CIFAR only
eval.protocol: Test set shuffled before TTT-Online; no significance tests; seeds not reported except 'multiple independent trials'.

evidence.quote: we use stochastic gradient descent with the learning rate set to that of the last epoch during training, which is 0.001 in all our experiments

limits: Only image classification with a rotation-prediction auxiliary task; the authors say the auxiliary task must be well defined and non-trivial (airplane class shows no gain).
Computational cost is high: test-time slowdown of 2 x batch size x iterations; efficiency left to future work.
Online version assumes test samples come from the same or smoothly changing shifts; it did not work with Batch Normalization, forcing Group Normalization.
Theory covers only smooth convex models; deep nets are supported empirically (Fig 4).
CIFAR-10.1 gain is small relative to the drop (authors concede).
Joint-training hyperparameters (batch size, epochs, lr schedule) are not stated in the paper; no seed counts or confidence intervals.
Paper text refers to a thresholding trick 'introduced in the method section' (Appendix A2) that this version's method section does not contain.

terms.definition: Fine-tune the shared feature extractor by minimizing the auxiliary self-supervised loss on a single unlabeled test sample before predicting
Online version where theta for x_t is initialised from theta(x_{t-1}) rather than reset
Baseline trained on main and self-supervised tasks but fixed at test time
Model parameters theta(x) depend on the test sample x but not its label

lineage.note: Paper is a follow-up; compared as oracle baseline

Unsupervised representation learning by predicting image rotations (Gidaris et al.)

Do CIFAR-10 classifiers generalize to CIFAR-10? (Recht et al.)

lineage.note: Key inspiration: learning at test time on the input itself

code.snippet: joint: min over (theta_e, theta_m, theta_s) of 1/n sum_i [ l_m(x_i,y_i;theta_m,theta_e) + l_s(x_i;theta_s,theta_e) ]; test time: min over theta_e of l_s(x;theta_s,theta_e), then predict with (theta_e*, theta_m)
